title: Probabilistic commit intake and runway estimator for Dedicated capacity provisioning
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
Teams requesting Dedicated capacity today open a reservation that often requires manual back-and-forth to size throughput, align SLAs, and choose autoscaling profiles. This causes long lead times, conservative overprovisioning, and capacity churn.

Goal:
Design and deliver an intake workflow and approval policy that: (1) auto-sizes small commitments with a probabilistic runway estimator, (2) surfaces clear approval tiers and decision gates for larger requests, and (3) plugs into autoscaling policy templates so Dedicated fleet controls are provisioned with correct defaults. The intent is to reduce manual approvals for low-risk requests, improve forecast accuracy for capacity planning, and reduce average provisioning lead time by 35%.

Scope and boundaries:
- Intake form and backend validation logic (policy engine) for new commitment requests.
- Runway estimator service that consumes historical usage/peaks, SLOs, and requested throughput to compute a 95% and 50% runway (time until commit likely needs top-up) as a probabilistic forecast.
- Approval rules: auto-approve commits <= X qps and <= Y months predicted runway; manual approval for > thresholds.
- Integration points: Redwood Console for request submission, Slack/email notifications to capacity team, inventory ledger for fleet allocation.
- Out of scope for this ticket: long-term billing contract language and legal signoffs.

Key acceptance criteria (high level):
- Intake form fields cover: expected avg qps, burst qps, target p50/p95 latency SLO, expected traffic pattern (cron/steady/spiky), expected retention period, beta vs GA classification, and contact owners.
- Runway estimator returns a human-readable summary and numeric estimates: 50% runway, 95% runway, and top-3 drivers (e.g., daily burst, hourly peaks).
- Auto-approve policy implemented and configurable by tier: default thresholds documented and editable by Capacity PMs.
- Approval workflow generates a single source-of-truth artifact in the capacity ledger with allocation id and initial autoscale profile.
- Dashboard panel in Console shows pending approvals, estimated runway distribution, and confidence bands for forecasting.
- End-to-end tests that validate auto-approval path and manual escalation path.

Design decisions and trade-offs to be considered:
- Conservative default thresholds vs more aggressive auto-approve to reduce latency. We propose conservative defaults for GA and an opt-in relaxed mode for low-risk internal teams.
- Probabilistic model accuracy vs explainability. Use a simple Bayesian bootstrap-style estimator first (fast, interpretable), with a plan to replace by a more advanced time-series model once we have labeled outcomes.
- Placement of policy enforcement: central policy service vs console-side checks. Implement central policy service to avoid divergence across clients and console versions.

Deliverables:
- Intake form wireframe and final fields (Console) — linked in artifacts.
- Policy engine implementation (feature flagged).
- Runway estimator microservice with a simple API returning runway estimates and confidence quantiles.
- Approval routing rules and on-call rotation for manual escalations.
- Console dashboard tiles for Capacity team.
- Documentation: PRD, operator runbook, and user-facing "how to request Dedicated" guide.

Success metrics (leading and lagging):
- Leading: % of commits auto-approved, median time from request to allocation, forecast-to-actual variance at 7 and 30 days.
- Lagging: Average provisioning lead time reduction vs baseline, reduction in overprovisioned capacity measured in GPU-hours.

Notes on privacy and compliance:
- Request metadata may contain customer identifiers; ensure ledger entries are stored in the customer tenancy where required by policy and PII controls are enforced.
- No model training data will be exported with customer data for runway estimator MVP.

Implementation timeline (rough):
- Week 1: finalize intake schema and approval thresholds; wireframes for Console.
- Week 2: policy engine skeleton, runway estimator MVP (bootstrap model) + minimal API.
- Week 3: integrate auto-approve flow and ledger write path; Console submission link.
- Week 4: dashboard and E2E tests; staged rollout and A/B safety gate.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form captures all required fields and validates client inputs
Runway estimator returns 50% and 95% runway with confidence bands
Auto-approve policy applies to requests matching default thresholds and writes allocation record
Manual approval path notifies capacity on-call with contextual summary and one-click approve/deny actions
Console dashboard surfaces pending requests and forecast variance for allocated commitments
E2E tests cover both auto-approve and manual approval flows
